summary: Discovery call to understand Sienna's constraints for adopting Redwood: quick time-to-first-token (TTFT) via PLG/self-serve, evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) for security and latency, and next steps to pilot with credits and run benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey, everyone, thanks for hopping on. i'm Maya, account exec for the east coast, and with me is Samir, our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:06] Olivia (Sienna CTO): Olivia here, and Marcus, Leah and Diego are with me. thanks Maya.
[00:10] Marcus: Hey.
[00:12] Leah: Hi.
[00:15] Samir (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. agenda — we'll ask about your current infra and goals, talk about our PLG onramp (credits + TTFT playbook), then high-level hosts: hosted, dedicated, private, and close with next steps. Sound good?
[00:27] Olivia: Sounds good. We're short on time but yes.
[00:30] Maya: Perfect. Marcus, can you give us a quick background: what are you trying to build and why are you evaluating hosted vs private?
[00:37] Marcus: Sure. Sienna's building a customer support augmentation layer, summarization + response generation, and we also have an internal code-assist. main constraints: PII in logs, latency targets under 250ms for short responses, and predictable costs. We're a small team so TTFT is important — we like the idea of free credits to spin up something fast.
[00:55] Diego: also, we already host infra in GCP us-east1, but we run some batch workloads on-prem. curious about dedicated GPUs vs your hosted multi-tenant for both performance and cost.
[01:08] Maya: Great — that's the classic tradeoff. quick note: our PLG credits are meant to get you to first request in hours; our time-to-first-token playbook includes a sample repo, a curl example, and a tiny starter app. we'll send the link after the call.
[01:22] Leah: On security: we're SOC2 in progress, and SSO is a hard requirement (SAML). we need audit logs and customer-managed keys if possible.
[01:31] Samir: Yep, all supported. we have SOC2 Type II docs, SAML/SSO integrations, and we can do KMS integration for keys in our Private offering. Note: private can be VPC-hosted with a private control plane or full on-prem if needed.
[01:45] Olivia: what's the gap in effort for dedicated vs private? like how many engineers do we need to allocate?
[01:51] Maya: For Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) we manage the infra and you get isolated capacity; setup is usually 2-4 weeks for initial provisioning and network peering. Private (VPC/on-prem) takes longer — typically 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and network/firewall work. but if you want TTFT for an internal pilot, hosted is the fastest.
[02:08] Marcus: Can you quantify cost roughly? Our finance wants a ballpark to model.
[02:12] Maya: We'll send tailored pricing; high level: hosted is usage-based (per-token + embeddings), dedicated is committed monthly capacity with lower unit cost, and private has platform fee + support. i'll add numbers in the email.
[02:25] Diego: For the hosted path — are there rate limits? we want to run a short POC that gets bursty.
[02:30] Samir: Hosted supports burst and autoscaling within limits; we can negotiate dedicated burst windows. for strict throughput, Dedicated or Private is better.
[02:39] Marcus: Okay. what about model variants and fallbacks? We may want to degrade gracefully if capacity is constrained.
[02:44] Samir: We do smart routing, yes. policy based: latency-first or cost-first. we can configure automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants — honest note, quantized outputs sometimes need re-evals for quality.
[02:59] Olivia: Re- evaluations, yeah that's a concern for us — we need consistent output for compliance.
[03:05] Samir: Understood. We have eval tooling integrated in Redwood Optimize to flag regressions per prompt set — we'll include an example.
[03:12] Leah: Can we keep logs in our own account? Data residency?
[03:16] Maya: For hosted, we manage logs but have retention controls and can redact PII. For Dedicated, logs live in the tenant; for Private, you control storage. we also offer an option for customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:31] Marcus: You mentioned KV cash earlier in your docs — how does that work?
[03:34] Samir: (laughs) KV cache — sometimes the transcript flips. it's the KV cache for transformer states; it speeds up streaming responses for repeated prefixes. it's automatic in dedicated/private and on hosted when we detect similar session patterns, though prefix caching behavior needs careful handling for privacy and consistency.
[03:52] Olivia: What's a reasonable size for the initial pilot? we want to test both latency and cost.
[03:58] Maya: Typical pilot: 1000-5000 requests/day for 2-4 weeks. we give PLG credits to cover that. the TTFT playbook gets you from zero to first call in under 4 hours if you follow the repo and cURL snippet.
[04:12] Diego: Are there SDKs for our python/Go stack?
[04:15] Samir: Yes — official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go, plus raw REST. the repo has example code.
[04:21] Marcus: For latency under 250ms, do you have benchmarks?
[04:25] Samir: We have verified perf profiles across model families in our catalog — smaller models on dedicated GPU pools can hit <100ms for short sequences. i'll note: final latency depends on batch sizing, prefix cache hit rates, and network egress. we'll run a quick benchmark during the deep dive.
[04:44] Olivia: Do you support SSO & RBAC? We need role separation for developers vs ops.
[04:49] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO and RBAC with token scoping and per-route permissions. plus audit logs and per-token cost breakout in Console.
[04:59] Leah: About encryption — can you describe the KMS flow quickly?
[05:03] Samir: Customer-managed keys: Private supports bringing your own KMS; we integrate with AWS/GCP KMS or HSM. keys manage model artifacts and encryption at rest. for hosted, we also support envelope encryption with customer keys in some enterprise plans.
[05:19] Marcus: How will the rollout work for model versioning? We need canary and A/B tests.
[05:24] Samir: We have rollout primitives — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. you define traffic split and model pins in the Console or via API.
[05:33] Olivia: Great. Security pack? you said you'd send docs.
[05:36] Maya: Yes, i'll send our SOC2 + architecture diagrams and a link to the security pack: https://redwood-inference.example/security-pack (note: placeholder).
[05:46] Marcus: For the pilot, what acceptance criteria should we define?
[05:50] Maya: Usually: 1) ttft under 4 hours from sign-up to first successful request, 2) latency SLA for 95th percentile under X ms for sample workload, 3) cost per session within expected bounds, 4) no PII leakage in logs. we'll help you design the test harness.
[06:07] Diego: Any specific network ports or rules we need to open for a VPC peer?
[06:11] Samir: We use standard TLS over 443 for API. for VPC peering we exchange CIDRs and set up peering; if you're on-prem we'll use a VPN or private link. i'll send a network checklist.
[06:23] Olivia: ok. curious — if we start hosted with credits and like it, how seamless is moving to Dedicated or Private?
[06:29] Maya: We designed migration paths to be smooth — same API and SDKs, model pins move across. Dedicated can be provisioned and you migrate traffic gradually via Console rollouts. Private is a separate deployment but we support data export and model version parity.
[06:44] Marcus: Are there any gotchas around tokenization differences across models? we sometimes see differences in token counts.
[06:49] Samir: Yes, tokenization varies by model family. cost estimates are model-dependent. we'll include tokenization notes and a small script to estimate tokens for your prompt shapes.
[06:59] Leah: From compliance side: can we get all audit logs for a timeframe? retention policy?
[07:03] Maya: Yes - retention configurable; for Dedicated and Private you can set long retention and export logs to your SIEM.
[07:10] Olivia: okay, i'd like to see a sample pilot SOW and pricing tiers.
[07:14] Maya: We'll send both after the call.
[07:17] Diego: about benchmark — can you provide a minimal harness we can run from our cluster? we want reproducible latency numbers.
[07:23] Samir: Absolutely. i'll provide a load test harness, sample prompts, and instructions to run both hosted and dedicated tests, plus expected baselines.
[07:33] Marcus: For PII redaction — automatic or do we manage?
[07:37] Samir: We offer both. you can use automatic redaction in transit and at rest, or do client-side redaction before sending. for compliance heavy use cases we recommend client-side redaction and Private.
[07:49] Olivia: One more — any references of similar customers in fintech or healthcare?
[07:53] Maya: We have references; i'll share case studies. note, we can't share identifiable PII but we'll provide anonymized benchmarks.
[07:59] Marcus: timeline wise — we need something within Q1 next year.
[08:03] Maya: That aligns well. pilot in Jan could convert to Dedicated in Q2 if performance/cost match.
[08:09] Leah: ok. let's talk about next steps and owners.
[08:12] Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing and pilot SOW, security pack link, and Samir will send benchmark harness. we'll schedule a 60-min technical deep dive next Wednesday, is that Wed 12th ok?
[08:23] Olivia: Wed 12th works.
[08:25] Diego: yes.
[08:27] Maya: Great. i'll follow up with calendar invite and the package. thanks everyone.
[08:31] Olivia: Thanks.
[08:33] (call ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional word swaps (e.g., "KV cash"), timestamps are approximate; some speakers overlapped briefly.
